option_differences.question: Is there radiolucent gas beneath the right hemidiaphragm, especially anteriorly near the xiphoid, indicating pneumoperitoneum?

option_differences.attribute: tracheal integrity and contour (lumen interruption vs. angulation vs. normal)
option_differences.question: Does the tracheal lumen show abrupt cutoff or sharp kinking—suggesting rupture—rather than just shift or compression?

plan.task: Determine spatial relationship (location, size) between bronchiectatic changes and consolidation on chest imaging
plan.anatomy: Lungs, specifically lobes involved by bronchiectasis and consolidation

option_differences.attribute: lobe location of bronchiectasis
option_differences.question: Are the bronchiectatic changes predominantly in the left lower lobe or right lower/upper lobe?

option_differences.attribute: relative size and lobe of consolidation
option_differences.question: Is the consolidation in the right middle lobe or left lower lobe, and how does its size compare to the bronchiectatic region?

missing_attributes: clear demarcation of consolidation vs. bronchiectasis on CT slices

plan.task: Assess lobar distribution and symmetry of reticulonodular opacities, and presence of pleural effusion or mediastinal shift
plan.anatomy: Thorax, bilateral lungs, pleura, mediastinum

option_differences.attribute: lobar predominance and symmetry
option_differences.question: Are the reticulonodular opacities predominantly upper-lobe, lower-lobe, or diffuse without lobar predominance?

option_differences.attribute: pleural effusion presence and laterality
option_differences.question: Is there a noticeable pleural effusion, and if so, on which side?

plan.task: Compare two chest X-rays to assess temporal change in cavitated pulmonary nodules and their relationship to rheumatoid arthritis
plan.anatomy: lower lung zones, particularly left lung base

option_differences.attribute: size change of cavitated nodules in left lung base
option_differences.question: Do the cavitated nodules in the left lung base increase, decrease, or remain stable over time?

option_differences.attribute: location of new cavitated nodules (upper vs lower lobes)
option_differences.question: Are new cavitated nodules appearing in upper lung fields, or are existing ones in lower lobes progressing?

missing_attributes: presence/absence of pleural effusion or other RA-related features

plan.task: Identify visual differences between two CT images (pre- and post-treatment) to support diagnosis of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP) and its response to corticosteroids
plan.anatomy: thorax, lungs (bilateral peribronchovascular regions)

option_differences.attribute: spatial distribution and morphology of pulmonary opacities
option_differences.question: Do the opacities show bilateral peribronchial consolidation with air bronchograms in the first image, and significant reduction with residual ground-glass opacity in the second?

option_differences.attribute: temporal change in lesion extent and density
option_differences.question: Is there near-complete resolution (B), partial resolution with ground-glass residua (C), or no change (F)?

plan.task: Differentiate conditions based on chest X-ray findings in a child with sudden respiratory distress, soft tissue edema, and crepitus
plan.anatomy: Thorax, neck, subcutaneous tissues, mediastinum, lungs

option_differences.attribute: presence of linear radiolucencies tracking along soft tissues and mediastinum
option_differences.question: Are there lucent streaks extending from the neck into the upper thorax and along the mediastinal borders, suggesting air in subcutaneous and mediastinal planes?

option_differences.attribute: absence of pleural line displacement or lung collapse
option_differences.question: Is there no evidence of visceral pleural line separation from chest wall (i.e., no pneumothorax) or significant pleural fluid layering?

plan.task: Differentiate among differential diagnoses for a right upper lobe lesion in a patient with prior TB and haemoptysis, based on chest X-ray morphology
plan.anatomy: Right upper lobe lung parenchyma

option_differences.attribute: cavity morphology and internal features
option_differences.question: Does the lesion show a well-defined cavity with an air crescent sign (suggesting aspergilloma) or a thick-walled cavity without internal structure (suggesting TB or abscess)?

option_differences.attribute: presence of adjacent fibrosis/pleural tethering vs. mass-like opacity
option_differences.question: Is the lesion associated with volume loss, pleural thickening, and fibrotic bands (favoring post-TB cavity) or is it a discrete, possibly spiculated mass (favoring carcinoma)?

plan.task: Compare two chest X-rays to identify evolution of pulmonary findings in Churg-Strauss Syndrome
plan.anatomy: Thorax, lungs, hilar regions, lung lobes

option_differences.attribute: location and progression of consolidation
option_differences.question: Does consolidation start unilaterally (left) and become bilateral/diffuse?

option_differences.attribute: side and lobar distribution (left perihilar vs right upper lobe)
option_differences.question: Is there new right upper lobe consolidation appearing while left perihilar consolidation persists?

missing_attributes: side labeling (patient left/right vs image left/right)
exact lobar boundaries on PA CXR without lateral view

plan.task: Differentiate pneumomediastinum vs. pneumopericardium based on spatial extent and relationship to cardiac silhouette and neck
plan.anatomy: mediastinum, pericardium, cervical soft tissues

option_differences.attribute: spatial extent of pneumomediastinum (neck extension)
option_differences.question: Does air extend from mediastinum into cervical soft tissues?

option_differences.attribute: relative size and distribution: pneumomediastinum vs. pneumopericardium
option_differences.question: Is pneumomediastinum more extensive than pneumopericardium, or vice versa?

missing_attributes: exact boundary of pericardial air vs. mediastinal air
presence/absence of pleural effusion or mediastinal fluid

plan.task: Differentiate drug packet types based on radiographic density and morphology in oesophagus and intestine
plan.anatomy: oesophagus (C6-C7 level), small bowel

option_differences.attribute: radiodensity and internal texture
option_differences.question: Do the packets show homogeneous high density (suggesting crystalline solids like cocaine/heroin) or lower, heterogeneous density (suggesting plant material like hashish/marijuana)?

option_differences.attribute: shape and size consistency across locations
option_differences.question: Are the oesophageal and intestinal packets similarly sized and oval with smooth contours (typical of tightly wrapped drug packets) vs. irregular or fragmented (suggesting non-drug or degraded plant matter)?

missing_attributes: presence of air interfaces or layered appearance

plan.task: Differentiate among six diagnostic options based on chest X-ray findings
plan.anatomy: Thorax, including trachea, bronchi, heart, pulmonary vessels, and lung parenchyma

option_differences.attribute: Right-sided tracheal bronchus vs. cardiac/vessel anomaly
option_differences.question: Is there an anomalous bronchus arising from the trachea on the right side, or is there evidence of cardiac enlargement with abnormal vascular opacities?

option_differences.attribute: Presence/absence of pulmonary varix or sequestration (focal parenchymal lesion) vs. normal appearance
option_differences.question: Is there a focal rounded opacity in the left middle lung field suggestive of a varix, or a dense non-vascularized mass suggesting sequestration?

missing_attributes: Vascular contour detail (e.g., anomalous vein course)
Bronchial branching pattern at carina (requires CT for definitive assessment)
Cardiac chamber size quantification (e.g., cardiothoracic ratio)
Parenchymal density heterogeneity (subtle sequestration or varix may be obscured)
